subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw core add Anthropic pace tracking/throttling for autonomous agents, and should the first slice be read-only visibility, opt-in enforcement, or a plugin/API seam?
rationale: The remaining work adds provider-specific semantics, persisted state, new config/default behavior, status/session_status output, and autonomous throttling policy that source inspection cannot choose safely.

options.title: Scope core visibility first
options.body: Capture or normalize pace-relevant provider usage into status/session_status without blocking agent or subagent work until the data model proves reliable.

options.title: Add opt-in enforcement now
options.body: Introduce disabled-by-default pace thresholds that throttle subagents or non-interactive work with explicit upgrade, recovery, and miscalibration tests.

options.title: Design plugin/API hooks first
options.body: Keep core lean by defining generic provider and agent hooks so a plugin can own Anthropic-specific pace policy without hardcoding it in core.

recommendation.title: Scope core visibility first
recommendation.body: Capture or normalize pace-relevant provider usage into status/session_status without blocking agent or subagent work until the data model proves reliable.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest merged history across provider usage, status, and plugin usage hook surfaces touched by the decision.
